question: Is nuclear power the fastest path to decarbonization?

sources.title: Nuclear Power and Secure Energy Transitions
sources.extractedText: Lifetime extensions of existing reactors are among the cheapest sources of additional low-emissions electricity; net-zero pathways roughly double global nuclear capacity by 2050.

sources.title: Nuclear Energy and Climate Change
sources.extractedText: Nuclear plants deliver large volumes of firm low-carbon power; France's 1974–1989 build-out remains the fastest national decarbonization of an electricity system on record.

sources.title: Levelized Cost of Energy+ Analysis
sources.extractedText: Unsubsidized utility-scale solar and onshore wind remain the cheapest new-build generation on a levelized basis, while new nuclear carries the highest LCOE range and the widest uncertainty band.

sources.title: Nuclear Energy — Our World in Data
sources.extractedText: Annual additions of solar and wind now far outpace nuclear, though nuclear's 1980s build rates remain unmatched per unit of firm capacity added.

sources.title: Projected Costs of Generating Electricity 2020
sources.extractedText: Plant-level LCOE comparisons omit system costs; once balancing and network costs are included, the cheapest low-carbon system is not simply the one built from the cheapest individual plants.
